title: On‑Prem Environment Mirroring Load Runner & Regression Detector
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an on-prem / VPC load runner that can mirror a customer's production environment and produce fully reproducible, deterministic benchmark runs for tokens/sec, p95 latency, and regression detection. The harness should support: (1) declarative scenario definitions (traffic mix, sequence length distributions, correlated KV cache warmup), (2) re-playable randomness seeds and fixture snapshots, (3) pluggable workload drivers (gRPC, HTTP/REST, Redwood API), (4) per-run artifact collection (trace spans, per-token latencies, GPU utilization), and (5) automatic regression scoring vs. baseline runs. This ticket covers the orchestration, deterministic input plumbing, and integration with Console dashboards + alerting for automated regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: A1: The runner can execute a named scenario in a private/VPC environment from a declarative YAML manifest and produce a single-run artifact bundle (metrics, traces, request logs, RNG seed).

A2: Measured metrics must include tokens/sec (aggregate & per-worker), p50/p95/p99 latencies, request QPS, and tail KV-cache hit ratios. Artifacts are uploaded to a central benchmark store for diffing.

A3: Given a baseline run id, the system produces a regression report that highlights percent changes in tokens/sec and p95 and computes a statistical significance flag (simple t-test or bootstrap) and a pass/fail status based on configurable thresholds.

A4: Harness supports a reproducible warmup procedure that can restore a recorded KV-cache snapshot before the measured window and verify determinism across 3 consecutive runs (<=2% variance in tokens/sec and <=5% variance in p95).

A5: Integration with Console: ability to push metrics and regression reports to the Console 'benchmarks' dashboard and raise Slack alerts when a regression is detected with a link back to the artifact bundle and suggested rollback policy.
A6: End-to-end smoke run documented in the runbook with Terraform templates to provision test harness infra in a sample VPC and an example scenario manifest included in the repo.
tasks: T1: Design scenario manifest schema (traffic mix, seq-length histogram, kv-cache snapshot pointer, seed)
T2: Implement deterministic RNG and fixture serializer (save/restore KV cache)
T3: Build drivers for HTTP and internal Redwood API (token accounting) with concurrency controls
T4: Metrics collector that aggregates tokens/token-second, per-worker latencies, GPU stats and exports to Prometheus/Pushgateway
T5: Regression scoring service (baseline diffing, statistical check, threshold config)
T6: Console integration: dashboard panels + alerting rule + linkback to artifact store
T7: Terraform test infra templates and runbook for on-prem/VPC deployment
T8: End-to-end validation and 3-run determinism test harness
notes: 2025-11-06: Spike completed to verify deterministic KV snapshots with current runtime—found non-determinism in quantized matmul kernels when using XLA-style autotuner; workaround will pin kernel selection during measured runs.

2025-11-08: Decided on YAML manifest v1 fields: name, description, driver, seed, warmup_snapshot, seq_length_histogram (percentiles), parallel_clients, request_template, duration_seconds. Kept manifest intentionally small to encourage composability.
2025-11-10: Performance goal: be able to detect a 10% regression in p95 with 90% confidence for 5-minute runs on a 4-GPU on-prem cluster. We may iterate on statistical test if runs are noisy.
2025-11-12: Integration plan with Console: push run metadata to /benchmarks API, store artifacts in S3-compatible archive with lifecycle, add 'last baseline' selector in dashboard to compare runs.
2025-11-14: Security review flagged secrets handling in fixtures; decided to require KMS-encrypted snapshots and ephemeral instance profiles for blob downloads.
comments: Marcus Nguyen (2025-11-09): Initial driver prototype can replay 100 concurrent clients against an internal test model; observed 12% variance in p95 on cold start but <3% after deterministic warmup.
